issues.detail: Coverage is mostly happy-path: there is no guidance on handling rate limits, API errors, empty retrieval results, or malformed structured output, and the fallbacks and cache snippets lack failure-mode discussion.

Both examples are prose descriptions of what the agent will build rather than concrete runnable input/output demonstrations, and the Example 2 SQL tool is described without any code or read-only enforcement beyond a mention.

scenarios.name: rag-with-persisted-chroma-mmr
scenarios.rationale: Response A covers nearly every rubric item (DirectoryLoader+PyPDFLoader, RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter 1000/200, Chroma persist_directory, MMR retriever with k and fetch_k, a cite-sources prompt, a Sources list from metadata, and an LCEL-style chain), while Response B uses none of the LangChain components, has no MMR retriever and no LCEL chain, and only matches the rubric on persistence, cited prompts and a Sources list.

scenarios.name: agent-with-tools-and-thread-memory
scenarios.rationale: Both use create_agent, @tool functions with docstrings, a provider:model string, InMemorySaver, thread_id config, and a {"messages": [...]} input, so both cover the rubric; A adds per-user access control through runtime context and Decimal refund math, which gives it a slight edge on detail.

scenarios.name: structured-extraction-with-fallback-and-batch
scenarios.rationale: Both define a Pydantic model with Field descriptions, use with_structured_output with a prompt via pipe, add a ChatAnthropic fallback, and set max_concurrency=5; A uses the sync chain.batch the rubric names and B uses abatch (sync only in a note), and A's Field descriptions are slightly less complete since sentiment has none.
